title: Nonunique nearest stable complex quadratics
author: Alec Kriebel
full_original_abstract: The closed set of complex monic quadratics with roots in the closed left half-plane is not prox-regular at z². For every fixed positive-definite real inner product on coefficient space, unstable quadratics with multiple attained global nearest stable quadratics occur arbitrarily close to z². The conclusion also holds in the full exact-degree quadratic coefficient space. A direct proof exhibits a limiting normal whose cubic support dominates a quartic squared displacement. The same obstruction disproves set prox-regularity of the whole abscissa epigraph. In contrast, the monic quadratic abscissa is function prox-regular at the origin relative to each finite limiting subgradient. Thus the historical question about local unique stable-polynomial projection has a negative answer for complex coefficients, while this example does not refute the separate function condition.

meta_description: A research note on nonunique nearest stable complex quadratics, fixed coefficient metrics, and the distinction between set and function prox-regularity.
accessible_explanation: Approximating an unstable polynomial by stable coefficients can give equally close answers. This note claims that such ties occur arbitrarily close to z² for complex quadratics under every fixed positive-definite real coefficient inner product. Stable means all root real parts are nonpositive, so imaginary-axis roots count. The argument uses the local geometry of the stability boundary and a classical theorem relating prox-regular sets to unique metric projection.
central_result: For each fixed positive-definite real coefficient inner product, every neighborhood of z² contains an unstable complex monic quadratic with at least two distinct attained global nearest closed-left-half-plane stable quadratics. The corresponding conclusion is proved in the note for full exact-degree quadratic coefficient space near (1,0,0), with a separate compact-localization argument for global attainment.
secondary_results: The note also claims failure of whole-epigraph set prox-regularity, while proving finite-subgradient function prox-regularity for the monic quadratic abscissa at the origin in the real Euclidean coefficient metric. Constants in the function statement may depend on the chosen finite subgradient.
limitations: Complex quadratics only; no general real-coefficient or all-degree classification.
For real monic quadratics, the stated closed stability set is the convex orthant a≥0,b≥0, with unique metric projection.
Every metric is fixed and positive definite; the result does not cover arbitrary norms, singular metrics or nonlinear parameter-metric transfer.
The nearest stable points are global and attained, but no explicit unstable input together with its two minimizers is supplied.
Finite rational and Decimal checks supplement analytic proofs; numerical controls are not interval certification or formal proof-assistant verification.
The Oberwolfach question omits field, normalization and metric. The historical comparison here uses Lewis’s explicit complex-coefficient convention.
No claim of firstness or of present-day openness is made.
